Engineering reference MVP2 / foundation

Native architecture

Three native processes, shared Swift packages, and separate authenticated UI and event transports.

Development previewMVP2 foundation complete. Local service and the synthetic API demo work locally. Live hooks, enforcement, and Anthropic BYOK are pending.

Current invited beta scope

This guide retains earlier milestone design and evidence. The current ten-tester beta preparation uses ad-hoc signatures and is not notarized. Production Cloud API deployment is verified; the signed native client connects through authenticated service IPC; genuine hosted inference remains pending. Claude Code 2.1.290 callback allow/deny, timeout, outage and exact-action native human review checks pass using a local model double; Codex coverage remains unverified. Earlier pending statements describe their original milestone. No public download is published.

Process responsibilities

ProcessResponsibility
TraceRook.appSwiftUI dashboard, MenuBarExtra, onboarding, UserNotifications, native review, settings
TraceRookAgentPer-user nonprivileged LaunchAgent: policy, model scheduling, approval deadlines, SQLite, health
tracerook-hookSigned arm64 CLI: bounded stdin, socket request, host output, shared catastrophic fallback

The app uses Swift 6 and standard Apple frameworks. There is no Electron or web view shell. The planned service registration uses a supported per-user mechanism with explicit consent. No service is registered in this milestone and no root daemon is part of the design.

How the components connect

  1. Claude Code / CodexA supported local lifecycle hook provides host JSON.
  2. Signed bridgeLength-prefixed JSON travels over a user-owned Unix socket.
  3. Agent serviceNormalize, inspect, redact, classify, and bind the exact action.
  4. Policy and providerLocal rules first; permitted selected context goes directly to Anthropic when needed.
  5. Approval and native UIAuthenticated XPC publishes status and accepts authorized review mutations.
  6. Host decision and historyReturn a host-compatible result; retain a sanitized, uncertainty-aware audit record.

Shared modules and concurrency

Contracts own versioned envelopes, enums, and provider-independent representations. AgentAdapters own host names and input/output mapping. Privacy owns redaction and minimization. Rules and Core own deterministic evidence, evaluation precedence, and state transitions.

Mutable stores, review coordination, analysis scheduling, and health monitors use actors. UI state is MainActor-isolated. Async/await carries deadlines and cancellation. The service alone writes SQLite; the UI reads through XPC rather than opening the live database concurrently.

Trust and transport boundaries

Host input and model reasoning are untrusted. The implemented bounded Unix socket checks kernel peer UID and running code identity. Authenticated XPC checks the intended signed family in both directions. Only XPC accepts review mutations; the hook socket rejects approval writes. Same-user malicious interference remains a coverage limit.

Local development builds explicitly pin the current ad-hoc app, service and helper hashes. This tests integrity and family matching; it does not establish publisher trust. Developer ID builds retain their strict certificate/team policy, which has not been tested with an available certificate.

The Local API Demo adds service-owned HTTP to a fixed loopback endpoint. It uses separate synthetic types and transient credentials. Fixture results cannot enter the live provider, approval, incident or coverage paths.

Repository layout

App/                         Native SwiftUI interface
Agent/                       Background service executable
HookCLI/                     Signed command-line bridge
Packages/TraceRookContracts/  Versioned strict contracts
Packages/TraceRookCore/       Policy, service, SQLite, mock HTTP
Packages/TraceRookIPC/        Authenticated local transports
Packages/TraceRookPrivacy/    Sanitization utilities
Packages/TraceRookAgentAdapters/
Packages/TraceRookFixtures/   Offline demo resources
backend/                     Isolated local mock and legacy API
Tests/                       Swift Testing harness
website/                     Static product site and docs

Native demo, service transport, durable state, and the connected local API demonstration work in this development checkout. Safe host installation, operational live enforcement, native Keychain-backed analysis and hosted Cloud remain pending. See the acceptance record.
